To whom much is given much is expected. There are professing Christians in this world who have never accepted the gift that God has extended to us. They've taken the offer and buried it and done nothing with it. They didn't take it in as their own and nurture it and use it to increase God's kingdom. 

Again this isn't a works-based salvation. If the unprofitable servant had taken his one talent of silver and kept it in his care, he'd still have been saved. But rather he buried it, and went through the motions. 

God goes out of his way in his indictment against Israel in **Psalm 50** to stipulate that His people who are righteous are protected under his care. His problem is with the false professors of His name who think that the formalism of their worship is sufficient to spare them from His wrath.

God's accusations against them are sharp. They can tend with thieves and are partakers with adulterers. Both the literal engagement with the worldly, and the spiritual, of general ecumenicalism. They speak evil things, and lie. They not only don't love their neighbors, but they lie against their own brothers. 

And God, God who is longsuffering and merciful and wood that all men come to repentance, gave them space and time to reconsider their ways. Instead they considered themselves holy, like God is Holy. They thought that in their religious practices, and keeping the letter of the law that they could ignore the purpose of the law and its spirit. 

It's the same indictment here as in **Matthew 23**. And it could be said Of so many supposed Christians today. 

It's interesting to me that **Hebrews 10** bookends the idea of being no more need for sacrifice for those in Christ, and there being no more sacrifice for willful sin, around the command to attend church. 

**Hebrews 10:23–25**
*Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

We are commanded to not forsake the assembly. And the purpose of that is to love one another. Edifying each other. Building each other up. So much more as the day approaches. 

But today, there are those who see church as a check box for their righteousness. Proving that they are holy as God is holy simply by their attendance. And in so many acts that they do, they wash the outside of the vessel, while inside they are whited tombs filled with dead men's bones. 

Those people to whom religion is a series of rituals and obligations that only benefit themselves, who see sacraments as their sacrifice rather than the blood of Christ. Christians in name only who go through the motions and never once consider God. 

They forget God and he will tear them to pieces. They bury their talent out of fear, while never truly fearing God. 

But God, ever gracious ends on a positive note. 

*Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.*

Our purpose of being his people is to praise his name that he be glorified among men. We are the salt of the earth. We are what is preserving the world against judgment. And so he's encouraging us to continue in that praise and thankgiving and glorifying God among men. 

Because it is possible for salt to lose its savor. For lukewarm Christians to have the candle of their church put out. To be of no further use of God so he calls you home if you're saved and if you're not, casting you into outer darkness. 

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

God's case against Israel is God's case against all who call themselves by His name and fail to live to proclaim His glory. 

Let us then stay salty, maintain our savor, do all things with Mercy and judgment forgiving those who trespass against us, considering the plight of the poor and the widow and the fatherless. Exhorting one another.

So that at the coming of Christ, when He brings firey judgment upon the world, We will be found acceptable. Where He will say that we are good and faithful servants. Amen

**Psalm 51** 
*Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.*

*2 Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.*

*3 For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.*

*4 Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.*

*5 Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.*

*6 Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.*

*7 Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.*

*8 Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.*

*9 Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.*

*10 Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.*

*11 Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.*

*12 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.*

*13 Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.*

*14 Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

*15 O Lord, open thou my lips; and my mouth shall shew forth thy praise.*

*16 For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.*

*17 The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

*18 Do good in thy good pleasure unto Zion: build thou the walls of Jerusalem.*

*19 Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.*

**Psalm 51** is the clearest and most sober cry of contrition and supplication for forgiveness by a believer, in the face of a judgment by the Almighty God, that we have in Scripture. 

It is David at his lowest. "A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba."

We know the story. David doesn't go off to war as kings were expected to. He stays at his place and sees Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier, Uriah the Hittite, bathing on her nearby roof. Filled with lust, he has her. And as a consequence of that adultery, David conspired to have Uriah killed in battle, and wed his pregnant widow. 

Nathan confronts the King, and the Lord curses David for his sin;

**2 Samuel 12:7–10**
*And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul; And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things. Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.*

The judgment of God was given, the child should die. 

**2 Samuel 12:14–15**
*Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die. And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.*

David fasts and prays and stays by the child's side, but in the end the illness takes the boy. 

**2 Samuel 12:18–19**
*And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.*

David, devastated, cleans himself and goes into the house of the Lord to worship. It is in this context that this Psalm was written.

Rather than a root of bitterness against the judgement of God, as many are tempted to take on in the face of such fierce judgement, David concedes and comes to the Lord, asking for mercy. As he has so often in **Psalms**, he begins in worship, praising God for His lovingkindness and mercy. Reminding himself, and the Lord of His great qualities, and appeals to the ultimate judge to blot out his transgressions. 

This is a formula of prayer that we should commit to our prayer life. Under better circumstances and joyous events, or in grave repentance and regret for whatever sins we have committed, the Lord should be approached in humility and meekness of spirit. Hallowing His holy name. 

The request is to forgive the confessed transgressions, knowing He is merciful and faithful to forgive His children. 

**1 John 1:9**
*If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness*.

This same promise applies to believers, today. The sure knowledge that our heavenly Father is faithful to forgive us, even the sins of the level of David. To wash us throughly, to cleanse us. To blot the iniquity from our record, and heal us, and our relationship with God. 

But note, it is if we confess our sins. David acknowledged his transgressions. We cannot lie to God and we should not lie to ourselves. We cannot hide from our sin when we've faced judgment, and our conscience keeps the sin ever before us in guilt.

The joy and benefit of the forgiveness of God comes in relief from that burden, and removing the fear of chastening, that comes from a contrite heart seeking His mercy. 

*Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight...that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.*

David confesses that it is the transgression towards God that out him in judgment, and so he admits to God that not only has he sinned against Him, but that David acknowledges his understanding that God's judgments are right and deserved. 

Again, it is very common to see people in sin, when facing the judgment of God for it, to grow to resent Him and despise His judgements. To make excuses for their acts, to deny their intent, to place what has resulted from their wicked ways on the shoulders of a God whom they reject as judge. 

These people are destroyed with their bitterness, wracked with guilt, have a broken relationship with the God that bought them, and are often called home early, the result of their being incapable of being honest and appealing to His mercy. 

But David shows us the better way.

David continues his confession; 

*Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.*

He uses hyperbolic language to say that he is a sinner, born of a sinner, in his appeal for mercy. 

There is much made of this passage, and all manner of doctrines that have been spun out of it. The primary being "original sin" as the idea that babies are born guilty, and condemned. 

But the very account being mentioned show that David did not believe any such thing. 

**2 Samuel 12:21–23**
*Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me*.

David, who knew he was redeemed by God, saved by faith, under the grace of the Lord, states plainly that he will go to be with his dead child in the end. That Heaven is their home. 

While Psalms are dripping with doctrine, we should still always compare scripture with scripture, and gain understanding by the totality of the Bible, rather than out of context proof texts.

Continuing in **Psalm 51**, having established the context and getting the contention on the false doctrine of original sin guilt that comes from a shallow reading of the text, we see the purpose of the Psalm is the honest confession of a righteous man. 

David is not placing the blame of what he has done on anyone else, and accepts full responsibility for whatever God judges against him. His fear of the Lord has led him to Godly repentance and reconciliation. 

*Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom*.

This is the meekness and honesty about our sin that God seeks, that in it, we can actually learn from Him and grow. 

We discussed in the previous **Psalm 50** study that God doesn't seek the sacrifices and burnt offerings, but a meek and contrite heart. He is pleased as a Father when we come to Him for restitution and forgiveness. His mercy and grace are limitless, all He asks for is honesty in our heart. 

*For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.*

David confesses, and calls upon the Lord to purge him with hyssop, the sponge like plant that was used to apply the blood on the posts during the first passover, the same that was present when the Lord was crucified and they gave Him gall to drink. 

The washing of forgiveness by the blood of Christ is ours, that we become white as snow. 

**Isaiah 1:18**
*Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.*

David pleads to be made to hear joy and gladness, to be cheered by the power of God's word to heal the brokenness he feels from the Father's chastening. 

He asks God to hide His face from David's sins. To see them and remember them no more. To blot out his iniquity. 

We know as saved Christians that this promise of God, to forgive our sins past, present and future, that He will remember them no more and place them as far from us as east is from west, is our blessed hope in the redemption that is found in Christ. 

We take comfort in this truth when we are faithful to confess to Him;

**1 John 1:7–10**
*But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.*

This promise shows not only the faithfulness of God to forgive, but also that our sin in the flesh is not held against our ledger in Heaven. It is not imputed against those that are in Christ. 

**1 John 3:9**
*Whosoever is born of God doth not commit sin; for his seed remaineth in him: and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.*

John is not contradicting himself by saying if we say we have no sin, we are liars and simultaneously saying we cannot sin, being born of God.

He is describing the same feelings from the failure of the flesh David writes about here. 

When we sin, it is not the new man, created in Christ, but the flesh. 

**Romans 7:15–17**
*For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I. If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good. Now then it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.*

Our flesh sins. If we deny that we are liars. But by being born again in Christ, we do not sin. The difference is that the flesh, which we can mortify to sin, and restrain from our lusts, is dead. Nailed to the cross with Christ. 

**Galatians 5:24–25**
*And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

Our spirit is quickened and covered by the imputed righteousness of Christ Jesus. It is His righteousness that covers our transgressions and the Spirit that seals us unto redemption.

So David, in his sorrow and remorse reminds God of this truth, and by doing so, reminds himself. 

*Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation and uphold me with thy free spirit.* 

David is not writing that he is afraid to lose his salvation, but seeking the confidence in it again that has been marred by his transgressions and the fear from the chastening he has received. 

He is seeking to renew his relationship with God through his confession and appeals to mercy. 

And the purpose? Is it to selfish ends of not wanting to feel guilty and to get back on the blessings side of God? No. 

*Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.*

It is the mercy God shows us as His children that leads us to share His praise to others, that the lost see His light upon us and they glorify Him in Heaven. It is not only the wrath that leaves the world without excuse, but the peace that passes understanding we are given by getting right with the Lord. 

When He delivers us from our guilt, forgiving our sin, restoring our relationship as sons, we cannot help but sing aloud of His righteousness. 

The sinner who trusts Christ is celebrated in Heaven by all the hosts of God...

**Luke 15:7**  
*I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.*

...How much more the prodigal son who returns to his Father?

**Luke 15:18–20**
*I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.*

The Father runs to meet his returning son, showering him with love. Before any confession of guilt or offer of penence or anything other than turning back towards God, the Father goes to him in comparison and restitution of their relationship. 

God wants to forgive us more than we want to be forgiven. And we rejoice in His grace, that we may shew forth His praise. 

Again, God doesn't want sacrifice. He doesn't want our works of penence and vows to change. He takes no delight in the ritual formulas of burnt offerings, and performative acts of contrition.

*The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.*

It is the healing of a loving relationship that He wants for us. Even at our lowest, we should remember this, and turn to Him again. 

It is then, in reconciliation and peace with God, through Christ Jesus our Lord, that the works we do and the praise we sing will please Him. Then will our religion match our hearts, in healing and in service to the mighty God. Amen

**Psalm 52** 
*Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.*

*2 Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.*

*3 Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.*

*4 Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.*

*5 God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.*

*6 The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him:*

*7 Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength; but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.*

*8 But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.*

*9 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.*

In **Psalm 52**, the psalmist presents the polar opposite of the contrite heart of **Psalm 51**, the mischief-making man who doesn't avail himself to the longsuffering mercy of God. 

The wicked and their deceitful tongue, inventing lies, telling slander against God and God's people, boasting of their blessings, not thankful but vain in their imagination, loving evil more than good, these are the men who continually reject the call to fear the Lord. 

Those of us who are saved can become incredulous at the prideful stance of the wicked, who reject the fear of God and lean on their own strength. We can often grow confounded and even depressed over the ways of the wicked. Like just Lot, living in Sodom, being afflicted by the wickedness around him

**2 Peter 2:8**  
(*For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

The Bible is not afraid to call these people out, directly and to their face. They are boastful, mockingly called "mighty men," liars, evil, haters of righteousness, lovers of slanderous and wicked words, lovers of mischief, having deceitful tongues. 

We should not fear to identify exactly the perverted in our midst when they reject and mock the gospel of God and the word we preach. 

Nor should we tiptoe around the heart of the matter; Their immanent destruction and the torment in the fire of Hell that awaits them. 

**Jude 1:22–23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: And others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

Those who do not see the wrath of God revealed from Heaven upon others as a reason to repent and believe, and won't see the mercy and hear the praise of the meek, feeling the compassionate love of believers magnify God's grace, need hard preaching to let them know exactly what they've chosen, in hopes that they might be saved. 

That their love of devouring words will lead to God likewise destroying them forever. Literally, being devoured by flame and worm in outer darkness, forever. Eternal suffering at the hands of a just and mighty God. 

*God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living.* *Selah*.

If "selah" is meant to be a pause, a moment to reflect on what was just sung or said, is there anywhere more fitting than in that moment, having heard that sobering truth? 

God will destroy you. He will take your life and root you out of the land of the living, to place you in a place of eternal destruction. 

And the righteous shall see their end and fear God, and laugh at the calamity they brought about on themselves. The end their mischief brought about, turned back upon them.

**Proverbs 26:27** 
*Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him*.

The ironic nature of the bitter end experienced by the boastful sinner is often evident and clear to those that fear God. The humor of the Lord is appreciated by His children. We laugh at their calamity. 

When the wicked are made a parable or a byword among the people, it should give other men pause. The wrath revealed from Heaven should give instruction to the simple to turn towards God. It shows the righteous in Christ God's power and promise. 

**Proverbs 1:7**
*The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

The warning is ignored by the fool. And God will not be mocked.

**Proverbs 1:25–30**
*But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof: I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh; When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD: They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.*

These men that did not trust in God, but made their own puny strength and their worldly, perishing riches their stronghold, will be brought low. By their evil deeds they seek to maintain power and control, and by the same they will be brought low by our God, Who is a consuming fire. 

But we are His. We have humbled ourselves to rely on His holy name. To be meek servants, poor in spirit, that we may receive His grace, and the abundance of life in His love. 

*I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints.*

They waited for Jesus, we look back to His cross and the glory of His resurrection. We shall praise His name among the people. We shall look at His mercy and wrath, and know He is our salvation. We will praise Him forever, as His saints. Amen

**Dispensationalism in light of the Book of Romans.** 

The events of the past week have seen an increase in the false claim that modern Jews occupying the Levant are the Israel of God, not saved believers. To defend this heretical garbage, those supporting this claim will use a handful of scripture, but they especially rely on **Romans 11:26**; 

*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob*

Stripped of context, this appears to support their false teaching, but luckily for us, we have the entirety of Romans to demonstrate why this interpretation is wrong, and frankly dishonest. 

For the next few days I am going to go over the building blocks for the arguments made by Paul in Romans to refute that reading of 11:26, once and for all. Starting today in **Romans 1**;

*Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God, (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,) Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ*

In **Romans**, the often abused epistle to the believers in Rome, Paul makes several arguments, and in the Spirit, these arguments build upon each other, each underpinning the next. 

Here in the opening greeting, Paul stipulated several important and fundamental points as a foundation of everything that follows. 

Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ, separated unto the Gospel of God. This is important. It isn't separation from; it isn't separation from the world, from sin, from his previous beliefs prior to salvation. It is towards something, with a purpose. And that something is not only the Gospel of Jesus in the sense we generally think of, the 4 books that tells us His life, teachings, death and resurrection, but Paul places the entire canon of scripture up to that point, the Old Testament as we refer to it, as the good news of God, because to Him all prophets gave witness. 

As Christ says;

**John 5:46-47** 
*For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?*

This is important to establish. Jesus being the fulfilment of the prophets and the oracles of God sets the context for everything that follows. Paul is going to give the final word on the Dispensation of Grace, and how it relates to both Jew and Gentiles. And this dispensation has been in effect from the beginning. It is of God, given in sundry times and diverse places to the fathers by the prophets, moved by the Spirit. 

The only new revelation is that it is Jesus who is called upon, the mystery of salvation that always existed, revealed in these last times, that all who call upon the name of the Lord are saved. 

The promise of God in Christ, His good news that He's been telling the patriarchs and the Hebrews in general, from the beginning, that Jews always had access to. They *should* know and have recognized who Jesus was. 

Paul then gives a concise rendition of that Gospel by which he and the Romans he is writing to (and we today), know we are saved:

-Jesus was **made flesh** through the seed of David 
-Declared **the Son of God** with power. Many signs miracles and wonders. Raising the dead and healing the sick. Preaching the word with authority, etc, **According to the Spirit of Holiness** 
-And **by the resurrection from the dead**
-**By whom we received grace**, apostleship, **called of Jesus Christ**. 

God became flesh and dwelt among us, was killed and raised from the dead as God promised, and all who answered the call are given the grace of God, the gift of eternal life. Called to follow Him and spread this good news to all nations.

Establishing this foundation that is Christ, the common faith shared between the Apostle and the assembly of believers in Rome, who have never met, but share this singular set of beliefs. Just as we who are saved today have believed. All who believe those truths are given eternal life. 

No works, no turning from sin, no other conditions making us worthy of the grace. And not by being a certain ethnicity or people. It is all excluded because it is in Christ we are saved.

*That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.*

That is the mutual faith, this recital of facts, the creed of the Gospel of Christ Jesus. Let us have comfort in that as we continue along. 

If you have added to this common faith, or taken from it, everything else that follows will offend you. Because the natural man receiveth not spiritual things. But, we who are saved and in agreement should be able to rightly divide the word of God as we move forward, comforted in this truth.

I should also make clear here at the beginning that I am only going to rely on clear scripture, being guided by the layout of Paul's thesis in Romans. 

I am not going to get too far into the weeds of endless genealogies and Jewish fables, of who the modern state calling itself Israel are. While I have opinions and there are many brothers with strong ideas one way or another, we don't need to get into it to provide understanding of the Jews in light of the Bible. So forgive me if I don't bring up these tertiary ideas, and take some others that are likely wrong at face value for the exercise.

The book of Proverbs is given to man, a gift of God with a very specific purpose. 

*To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding; To receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, and judgment, and equity; To give subtilty to the simple, to the young man knowledge and discretion.*

Much of the book of wisdom is by Solomon, who God gave an abundance of wisdom and knowledge and understanding, who as King displayed this wisdom in ruling, making Israel great again. But in his personal life, not so much. 

It is astounding how we, as men, can hear God's word, know His word, study it, hear it preached, and yet still lean on our own understanding, rather than in all our ways acknowledging Him that He may direct our paths. 

*A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels: To understand a proverb, and the interpretation; the words of the wise, and their dark sayings.The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.*

God's word should lead us to fear Him. To respect His holiness, power, mercy and justice. His wrath and His judgments. This is what makes a man wise, our fearful respect for the Lord, and being doers of the word, increases our knowledge and faith. 

Solomon writes, *My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother,* these truths are from God, and it is every parent's responsibility to teach them to our children, that they be an ornament of grace upon their head, and chains about their necks. It is the greatest inheritance we can give our children. It is also a command: Raising them in the fear and knowledge of God, to bring *them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.*

Continuing **Proverbs 1**, we see a warning against joining in another man's sin. Not being led to robbery and violence by greed. That ultimately, it ends in their own blood and death. Crime doesn't pay. 

Next, Solomon tells us of Wisdom, as a woman, though this is more the feminine of the word than a gendered being, and Wisdom is much like the Spirit of God, today. 

The original Hebrew word for wisdom, *hokhmah*, is a feminine noun, and Solomon will compare the virtuous woman of Wisdom to the harlot, the "strange woman," the folly of fools later in the book. 

But the literary device aside, like the male Spirit of God, He reproves and reproaches, and calls men to truth. Like God has done through the inspired word of the prophets, crying out, how long, ye simple ones? Scorners and fools reproofed. 

Wisdom is "poured out" in spirit. Calling us to repentance. God's words, the wisdom itself, made known unto us. As God promises to write the law in our inward parts.

**Matthew 23:37** *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

**Isaiah 65:2** *I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts*

What a sobering thing to be mocked of the Lord. To get to the place where you've been given up and given over. When you are destroyed in His presence, cast into eternal torment, and God will laugh, because He gave you ample warning. The wrath of God being revealed from Heaven, that you had no excuse. But they didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge.

But those who fear the Lord, and receive wisdom from Him, have a better promise;

Continuing in **Proverbs 3**, building on the understanding given already; that fear of God brings knowledge, His word brings discernment, and the Wisdom of God is the fruit of following His ways over our own. 

Following the way, walking His paths, being doers of the word and not hearers only, is Wisdom. But following other paths is like going in unto a strange woman, whose ways lead to death. 

But what are the advantages of knowing and keeping God's ways? Obeying His commandments? 

*For length of days, and long life, and peace, they shall add to thee*. 

God's commandments have promises. And it just makes sense that since the wages of sin is death, righteousness is life. 

Mercy and truth are the most precious of God's commandments. His mercy towards us shows the value of mercy to others. Truth guides us to judge righteous judgment. 

Jews today literally bind the words of the law to their arms, and in boxes on their forehead. They take the promise of finding favor of God and men for "binding" literally, and *omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith*.

*Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.*

This is the key verse of Proverbs. The foundational understanding. Remember it, sing it, say it. And in everything acknowledge God first. 

Be not wise in your own eyes, don't lean on your understanding. Don't think to blaze your own trails and beat down your own paths. There is nothing new under the Sun and God's ways are the best ways. The old paths, tried and true. 

And following them brings health. 

And honoring the Lord by giving of your substance, your riches, the first portion of your increase, will bring prosperity. 

Note this isn't a prosperity gospel, but show that gratitude for the blessings He provides, and acknowledging Him first, will see our blessing compound. He rewards gratitude and hates murmuring.

*My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; neither be weary of his correction: For whom the Lord loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.*

Gaining wisdom and understanding comes also from His chastening when we don't keep to His paths, when we stray to our own understanding. Like a mule that may wander off the path is whipped, so too are we chastened. And we should be thankful. 

**Hebrews 12:7-8** *ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.*

Be happy in chastening. Delight in His law. Gain understanding, covet Wisdom the way men covet riches, because it is more precious than silver, gold or rubies or any of the merchandise of the world. 

Wealth cannot extend your life and give you health, not like the Lord can. And love of money is the root of all evil, and for covetousness sake come wars. But pursuing Wisdom brings life. 

*Length of days is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and honour.*

Her paths lead to peace. Wisdom is a tree of life! So by faith we step out on the paths, and keep the commandments, understanding the promises of God.

The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth. Creation is by His knowledge and understanding. And knowing all things were created by His Word, through Christ Jesus, we see that Jesus IS the way, the truth, the light that is described throughout Proverbs. He is Wisdom. He is the tree of life. We are followers of the Way. We follow Jesus.

And so we keep His word, we study His ways, we keep wisdom and discretion, with the promo that He gives us life to our soul and lays grace upon our necks. Safety in our walk, and sure steps along His paths. 

Though we walk through the valley of the shadow of death, we have no fear. We lay down to sleep, and sleep the sweet sleep of those resting under the Good Shepherd. In the arms of Jesus. 

The Lord is our confidence.

Verse 27-32 can be summed up; Love thy neighbor. Give to him his due, good when it is in your power, loan to him freely when you can. Don't devise evil against him. Our neighbors dwell against us, locally. 

Jesus answers the question, "Who is our neighbor?" with the parable of the good Samaritan, leaning on this very wisdom. Our neighbors are those in our proximity who need help, and it is in our power to provide it. Love thy neighbor. 

Strive not with a man without cause. In the NT, Paul writes;

**Romans 12:8** *If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Love our enemies, certainly, but don't go out of your way to make one. Especially if they've done no harm to you. Don't be like the froward and oppressors, they are an abomination to the Lord. 

**FRO'WARD**, a. L. versus: *turned or looking from.*

- Perverse, that is, turning from, with aversion or reluctance; not willing to yield or comply with what is required; unyielding; ungovernable; refractory; disobedient; peevish; as a froward child.

Implacable, unmerciful, disobedient. It is as much an abomination to unreasonable and unyielding as being a sodomite, to the Lord. 

The Lord's curse will be on the house of the wicked. Vengeance is His. But the Lord blesses the household of the just. Those who work righteous judgement and show mercy. Peacemakers. The meek and lowly. 

This is wisdom. And as the meek inherit the earth and peacemakers are blessed, the wise shall inherit glory. 

While fools inherit shame.

Solomon continues giving the reader what is essentially a preface for the Book of Proverbs, that runs through chapter 9. The understanding of Wisdom vs folly, the good woman to be sought vs the strange woman, who leads to ruin. 

While there are plenty of wise sayings given in the first 9 chapters, including here in **Proverbs 4**, the thrust of Solomon's instruction is to emphasize this choice, and to encourage the pursuit of God's will, His paths, knowledge, discernment and Wisdom. 

He recalls his father David's instruction, stressing this idea. 

*Keep my commandments, and live. Get wisdom, get understanding: forget it not; neither decline from the words of my mouth. Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee. Wisdom is the principal thing*...

She brings honor, promoting the wise, and more importantly, leads to a crown of glory through the ornament of grace. 

The pursuit of Godly wisdom is inextricably linked to accepting the truth of God in His gospel. The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, but the end of it is grace and glory. 

Note the urgency of David in instructing his son, reflecting in Solomon's own words to his sons, and by the Spirit, to we who are sons of God. 

This should be every parent's priority, too.  Imparting this same understanding, that in wisdom is life, and that if you prioritize knowledge of God, you will not stumble, He will direct your paths, you have life in Him. 

Coupled with the warning to not follow after the wicked, the froward, the evil. Those who are only satisfied by mischief and by causing others to stumble. Taking pleasure in harming others. In violence. In offense. 

This is literally true, referring in previous chapters to those who rush to spoil and bloodshed. But it is also true of those who, rather than instruct children to go down the paths of Wisdom, instead mislead and bring children to offense. 

**Luke 17:2** *It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.*

And so, like David to Solomon, the king urges his children to not let these sayings depart from them. To keep them. To not turn to the left or the right. To keep our heart with all diligence. To ponder the path of our feet. In all our ways acknowledging God, that He may direct us where to go. To keep on the Way. To remove our foot from evil.

**Proverbs 5**
*My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding:*

*2 That thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge.*

*3 For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:*

*4 But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword.*

*5 Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.*

*6 Lest thou shouldest ponder the path of life, her ways are moveable, that thou canst not know them.*

*7 Hear me now therefore, O ye children, and depart not from the words of my mouth.*

*8 Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the door of her house:*

*9 Lest thou give thine honour unto others, and thy years unto the cruel:*

*10 Lest strangers be filled with thy wealth; and thy labours be in the house of a stranger;*

*11 And thou mourn at the last, when thy flesh and thy body are consumed,*

*12 And say, How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof;*

*13 And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!*

*14 I was almost in all evil in the midst of the congregation and assembly.*

*15 Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well.*

*16 Let thy fountains be dispersed abroad, and rivers of waters in the streets.*

*17 Let them be only thine own, and not strangers' with thee.*

*18 Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.*

*19 Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe; let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.*

*20 And why wilt thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, and embrace the bosom of a stranger?*

*21 For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord, and he pondereth all his goings.*

*22 His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cords of his sins.*

*23 He shall die without instruction; and in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.*

**Proverbs 5** continues the introduction section of the book of wisdom, and the near pleading of the father, Solomon, to his son, but in the Spirit, God the Father pleading with His children, to pay attention and listen to what He is teaching us. 

His instruction on chasing Wisdom, as knowledge and discretion, and warning of chasing after the strange woman of folly. 

But Solomon being the pen used by the Penman, the analogy given in this chapter of adultery serves as both a metaphor and practical application of chasing after women who aren't yours. Something the king with a thousand wives and concubines knows all about. 

So we can apply both literal and figurative and receive wisdom from both. 

The strange woman speaks sweet sayings, and is seductive in her ways, but her end is bitter and sharp. Deadly. 

God's paths are straight and knowable, a path of life, but her ways are moveable, ultimately unknowable. The Way is laid out and the light of that path is His word. The path of death shifts and moves and is full of snares and stumbling stones. Where you could think you know where you are and what lies ahead, and suddenly you're turned around and lost. 

In an adulterous relationship, this is also true. What may start in lust and be seen as temporary, often leads somewhere else, and far away. 

As they say: Sin will take you further than you want to go, keep you longer than you want to stay, and cost you more than you want to pay. 

Don't go looking for the strange woman. Don't seek out the folly of other men's understanding. It can cost you your honor, and take away years of your life to the service of the cruel, your wealth and labors to the stranger. 

Again, literally in the case of chasing after strange women, foreign women. Unsaved women. Women who are not your wife. 

In **1 Kings 11** we read, *king Solomon loved many strange women...he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart. For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.*

The wisest man in history, who wrote these warnings to his sons and to us, fell prey to the very thing he counseled against. 

Solomon may have written this in repentance and regret. He may have been in the midst of it. It could be before he succumbed to the temptation. But it is often true that the preacher preaches what he needs to hear, more than the audience. 

Verse 11 ties the literal back to the spiritual, and death and hell that awaits those who didn't fear God and seek after His Wisdom. The regret the fool will have as his flesh and body are consumed in never ending torment. 

*How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof; And have not obeyed the voice of my teachers, nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!* 

The shame in the midst of the assembly of being almost in all evil, when the books are opened in judgment...If physical death from a lifetime of bad choices and sin is heartbreaking, the regret in Hell for those that didn't harken to the gospel must be overwhelming. 

Solomon then compares fidelity to the wife of your youth, your first love, as with Lady Wisdom, to a fountain, to a well. To the cistern you dug. The waters are yours and you need not look for another source. 

*Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.*

Don't stray from your wife. Don't stray from the instruction of your fathers. Be ravished always with her love. Be satisfied in her. 

Our sins are before the Lord, He knows all our ways. A man's iniquities are the bonds he is caught in, the cords he is held with. Going after folly and rejecting instruction leads to a man's own sin binding him unto death.

He says such a woman is loud and stubborn and exists on every corner, just as folly and temptations are around every bend in the way.

She catches him, kisses him and saying she's holy, having made her offerings and confirming her vows, she beguiles him. Sheep's clothing for a ravenous wolf. 

She appeals with flattery, she sought him special, seeking to find only him, while she is a snare to any who cross her path.

She says the Goodman of the house is not home, and gone for a long journey...making it illicit and adultery. There likely is no "goodman" as a harlot keeps no husband. But there is an allegory here for sin and the temptation that judgment of God is afar off. The Goodman which is Christ, not here.

And so; *With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him.*

**Proverbs 8 (& 9)**, are an Ode to Wisdom, the Word and Spirit of God, with Him in the beginning , through Whom all creation was made. 

Wisdom cries out from all creation, from the top of the mountains, in the high places and in the paths. The Lord's way is wisdom. In the coming and going of the city. At its gates and doors. 

Like God calls to all men, as Jesus lifted up, wisdom calls out to all. To the simple and fools. To those who love wisdom and seek her excellent things, her right things. To those that seek truth. 

**John 14:6** *Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.*

**Matthew 7:7** *Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you*

**John 8:32** *And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free*

The words of wisdom are the word of God, and there is nothing perverse or froward in them. Holy and plain to those that listen. 

More precious than any treasures, wisdom is better than gold. With wisdom dwells prudence; Wisdom applied to practice. Discernment and action according to knowledge. 

The wise hate evil; pride and arrogance, froward mouths they hate.

By wisdom kings and princes rule. 

*I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me*.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. 

**Psalm 63:1** *O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is* 

The Lord's wisdom is from everlasting, His word. Before all creation, He is. Eternally with Him, as one brought up together. 

**John 1:1-2** *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God.*

Blessed is the man who finds wisdom. They receive life and favor of the Lord. They live in His grace. 

But woe to those that hate wisdom. *All they that hate me love death.*

**Proverbs 9** concludes the preface of Proverbs, the instruction of Solomon to his son on Lady Wisdom and the strange woman of folly.

The main themes presented in chapter 11 see the ways of the righteous compared to the transgressor, in matters of finance, fortune and benefit, and spiritual gain. 

The delight of the Lord in our keeping of integrity and honesty in our dealings. Just measures, not cheating others, being upright in our dealings. God places an emphasis on our doing well for others when we could, in secret, selfishly gain at their expense. Doing good when no one is watching, while the froward man's perverse ways destroy them. 

He warns that pride leads to shame and humility shows wisdom. How often have we seen pride lead to an almost immediate fall? In our own lives alone! Embarrassed and ashamed when we are puffed up. But walking in humility, we receive glory from God and others. 

Solomon's wisdom shows a repeated contrast between the righteous being delivered and the wicked destroyed. That the generosity of the righteous builds up more wealth, the liberal soul made fat. Not only in this life, but the next. 

*Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death,* reminds us that at the judgment, all the wealth in the world will do nothing to spare the wicked from wrath. Only the righteousness that is in Christ can. We are not appointed to wrath, by His mercy and imputed righteousness. 

*The righteous is delivered out of trouble, and the wicked cometh in his stead.*

And so we should put the Kingdom first in our hearts;

Matthew 6:19-21
*Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.*

A warning that those that hoard and withhold being generous, or not selling their excess, will lead to poverty and worse in the day of judgement. 

God loves a cheerful giver and sees fair and just enterprise as good. But hoarding and coveting, helps no one.

**Luke 12:16-21**
*And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.*

In the judgment, the hope of the wicked perishes, they shall not go unpunished. Their expectation is wrath. While the just and righteous shall be delivered. 

The righteous, those who are fair, just, walking upright, speaking truth, walking in the way of the Lord, not only benefit themselves, but their community. Their city rejoices in them. They bring prosperity to their people. They are a blessing. 

The wicked, however, curse their neighbors and overthrow their city. Being void of wisdom and unable to give counsel, despising their neighbors, bring destruction. They reveal secrets and are quick to mischief, and people suffer for their evil.

*He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it: and he that hateth suretiship is sure.* 

In **Proverbs 6**, we saw Solomon warning against surety, for a friend or a stranger, and here we see a similar warning. The seeming contradiction, that one who disfavors backing another's debts is seen by God as more sure than one who gives their pledge for a stranger. That they will regret it. 

The only surety we can count on is God's. In scripture the Holy Spirit is described as the "earnest" or seal guaranteeing a believer's eternal inheritance and salvation. The surety of our eternal life. 

**Ephesians 1:12-14**
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Because our surety is covered by the finished work of Christ, and sealed by the ernest payment of the Spirit, we can count on it. 

But for the stranger, we shall smart for it.

Finally, we are also given instruction in character. That gracious women are honorable, but women without discretion are not. That strong men retain their riches and merciful men do themselves good. 

*The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward.* How do we scatter righteousness? Winning souls. 

*The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; and he that winneth souls is wise.* 

The spiritual application to being one who scattererth, sowing righteousness, winning souls and bearing fruit, not hoarding our corn but blessing others...is again agrarian language as a parable for spreading the gospel. The greatest wisdom and counsel one can share. A blessing to those that receive it, and laying up treasure in Heaven for those that freely give it. 

And this is the promise of God for our efforts; *Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.*

Much of the chapter gives a contrast of the righteous and the wicked. The fruit of righteousness produces a stable, life-giving outcome: right and just thoughts, words that deliver and bring deliverance, enduring houses and legacies that stand firm, wisdom that earns commendation, compassionate regard even for beasts, roots that yield true fruit, escape from trouble, satisfaction from good speech and diligent hands, truth that establishes forever, joy for those who counsel peace, protection from evil, delight in the sight of God, excellence over neighbors, and ultimately leading to eternal life without death.

While the fruit of the wicked proves destructive and fleeting: deceitful counsels, words that lie in wait for blood and ensnare through transgression, overthrow and utter disappearance, perverse hearts deserving despise, cruel even in pretended mercy, desire only for evil nets, snaring by their own lips, momentary lying tongues, hearts filled with imagined evil and mischief, abomination through lying lips, seductive ways that lead others astray, and a path ending in no lasting good and death.

**Proverbs 13** opens and closes with very similar sayings, bookended thoughts that go well together. 

*A wise son heareth his father's instruction...He that spareth his rod hateth his son. A scorner heareth not rebuke...He that loveth* his son *chasteneth him betimes.*

 These concepts all go together. A scorner is that way because his father didn't love him enough to scourge him. A wise son listens because his father cared enough to apply the rod.

God is a loving Father. When we have forgotten the instruction of our parents, when we wander from His paths and neglect His word, we are rebuked of Him. If we aren't, we should wonder are we sons or bastards. Are we wise sons or scorners?

God ties our physical and spiritual fullness and satisfaction to our words; the righteous man speaking goodly words has what they need, but the wicked transgressors receive only violence and destruction, and are ever wanting. *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life, but he that openeth wide his lips*? Knowing to scatter the seed, in anticipation of a later harvest. Building up stores to the winter, but being generous with what you have, not being too short sighted to miss how that benefits you in the long run. How to wait patiently on the Lord. 

*The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul.*..*Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.* Hard work pays off. Quick riches fade but he that gathers by labor gains increase. 

Low time preference is the behavioral tendency to delay immediate gratification in favor of future, long-term rewards. It reflects a patient, disciplined, and forward-thinking mindset that values hard work, prudence, acquiring knowledge and understanding, and it is a sign of wisdom. 

The foolish are sluggards, they have high time preference and are easily tempted into sin. They covet, they seek mischief and violence, they gain their wealth by vanity, only to loose it. When they do store up against the future, they allow their greed to keep them from using it wisely, and it corrupts and rots, it's turned over to the just to recompense for evil, and is stolen or lost - *destroyed for want of judgement.*

Continuing in **Proverbs 14**, we are given several wise sayings, often repeating the points to really drive them home. Archetypes of wisdom contrasted with the folly of fools and warnings against liars. 

The wise builder, embodied especially in the "wise woman" of verse 1 who "*buildeth her house*," representing constructive, diligent wisdom that strengthens family, home, and community, where the foolish woman destroys her home, as plucking a hen. Bit by bit. 

Again, we are told the upright fear the Lord. This healthy respect for God is the source and substance of wisdom. But those on the crooked ways of the perverse hat the Lord. 

They have been made to know the truth, by the wrath of God revealed from Heaven against the ungodly, but they hate Him and truth. 

**Romans 1:28**
*And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient*

God will give the wicked what they desire, and by rejecting them utterly, give them over to their perverse ways to their own destruction. 

The fool speaks out because of pride, but the wise keeps their lips quiet when insulted. This is a hard one for many, including myself. Hard to remain quiet when being falsely accused and raised on or our pride is attacked. But Jesus showed us the way;

**Matthew 27:11-14** 
*And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, Thou sayest. And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. Then said Pilate unto him, Hearest thou not how many things they witness against thee? And he answered him to never a word; insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly.*

Humility in the face of accusations is often the most potent defense. Counterintuitive but like much of God's wisdom, it goes against man's understanding. 

*Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox.*

There are tradeoffs in life, and we are better for it. Sometimes, to get things done you have to be willing to shovel the dung. Another example of delaying gratification to your betterment. 

Faithful witnesses do not lie, but a false witness will. It seems obvious, and repeated in verse 25: *A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies.* When given the opportunity, we should remember the deliverance we received, and speak truth to deliver others. This is pleasing to God and foundational in the 10 Commandments. Thou shall not bear false witness. 

*A scorner seeketh wisdom and findeth it not...* reminds me of the false teacher, a reprobate who Paul describes in **2 Timothy 3:7** *Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.*

How can they, without the fear of God? How can they when they scoff at truth and hold it in unrighteousness? When they hate God rather than fear Him?

So we should reject the foolish man when you perceive he does not have knowledge. Again, flee a false prophet or someone claiming to know who just spouts nonsense. They ultimately will lie and speak falsehoods and defend their pride. They make a mock of sin, joking about evil ways. Flee these people. Don't take company with them, and don't try to sift any knowledge from them. They may be right about something, but in the end it isn't worth the rest that comes with it. 

*The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy.*

No one but you and God can know the heartache or the joy you feel in your heart. Truly know it. And you can't know another's, even when you empathize or rejoice with them. It's an important thing to keep in mind when others deal with you, or you're dealing with others. Have grace because of this limitation, and thank God for it, too. If our heart were open to men, it could be embarrassing and shameful. Thank God we don't actually wear our hearts on our sleeve.

Again, in verse 11 we see the wise builder's tabernacle flourishes when the wicked's will be overthrown. Not the structure, tent of building but the nature of the home. The family. 

*There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.* God's ways are not our ways. Our heart is deceitful and wicked. The things we think are right or the things of God we see as counterintuitive, often lacks perspective. Longview. Or are based on lies we tell ourselves to justify our sin. Prideful and graceless. Even the things we may laugh at, the Bible says, our heart remains sorrowful. Even in mirth is heaviness. Who can know man's heart?

And so, *The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself.* When we fall into sin, leaving the good path of the Lord, backslidding from whatever progress we have made, not walking in the Spirit but our own desires, we are filled with our own judgement.

*A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.*

We should be mindful of our heart, to keep it sound. To limit what we give into when we heed it. To know the spirit where what we desire comes from.

Remember the poor. Do not despise them, as we are poor in spirit and God gave to us abundantly. As Jesus said;

**Matthew 25:35-40**
*For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.*

And the promises of God to repay, that when we give to the poor we lend to the Lord.

**Psalms 41:1**
*Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.*

And again, in verse 32 we see the gospel in **Proverbs**, the righteous has hope in our death. That blessed hope of eternal life in Christ Jesus. This is wisdom, to hear and believe the truth of God's mercy and grace, by the imputed righteousness of Christ. 

Because righteousness exalteth a nation and sin is a reproach to any people, we should strive to win souls, instruct wisdom, have standards, that our nation would be blessed by our righteousness in Christ. Not Christian nationalism but a nation of Christians.

**Proverbs 15** begins by again establishing the truth that things we say, and the manner we say it, is a key instruction for holy living. 

A soft answer, given in kindness and grace can calm a situation. The tongue of the wise uses knowledge and disperses it. 

A wholesome tongue, speaking pure words is a tree of life. Both spiritually, by the gospel, but also metaphorically by lifting up others' spirit. Plans and purposes rely on wise counsel, and many counselors make them established. 

How we use our mouth, the words we choose, the knowledge we impart, the instruction we give, all is ultimately judged by God. 

**Matthew 12:36**
*But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment*.

Because of this, the grievous words that engender strife, stir up anger, or the mouth that pours out foolishness, all is ultimately vanity, and the man who hasn't humbled himself to the Lord, and received justification through Christ will surely be ashamed at the judgment. Imagine every foolish or wicked thing you've ever said in anger, read aloud by the holy God for all to hear. 

Every perverse word that causes others' spirit to fall. Every ignorant thing that led others astray. Every contention and strife stirred up by our unwise words, lack of discretion and wisdom, all revealed from the Great White Throne. 

I thank God for His great salvation, that spares me from such utter humiliation. This alone should convict man to repentance towards the gospel.

We see that even the thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to God, but pure words are pleasing to Him. A soft answer and pure words, instruction and knowledge, these please the Lord, and they are good to our soul, and are a blessing to the people in our life. 

*A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!*

How good it is to hear the joy of a brother when we are feeling down! The comfort in our mourning, being told exactly the thing we needed to hear, with all due wisdom and counsel, this is a gift to all, one we should spread ourselves.

The words we say, the things that our tongue forms and passes our lips, is a window to our heart. 

**Matthew 12:34**
*O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh*.

The heart of the fool prevents their lips from speaking wisdom. The heart one without understanding seeks foolishness to fill it, rather than understanding. The righteous' heart studies that they may give good answer to those seeking wisdom, but the wicked heart causes evil things to pour out the mouth of the fool. 

Every thought and word is known by God. 

*The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.*

The Lord is omnipotent and omniscient, ever present and knowing all things. Not only the words we speak, but the heart we keep. 

*Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?*

If the dead and hell are tormented in the presence of the Lamb, before God night and day, how much more our hearts are known by Him? 

**Psalm 44:21**
*Shall not God search this out? for he knoweth the secrets of the heart.*

The heart rejoices in the light of the eyes, a message of good report. Being the bearer of glad tidings, the reproof of life, the gospel...all this serves to brighten the heart of many, if they are inclined to wisdom and seek truth. Of course the fool rejects reproof and correction, to their shame.

The constant reminder from God to heed the wisdom of your father, to incline your ear to instruction, to prudently regard reproof continues to be hammered home. 

Following after the way of righteousness is wise, but those that have forsaken the way of God despise correction and hate reproof. Scorners hate being reproved of their ignorance. They won't seek after the wise. They feed on foolishness, are destitute of wisdom, their plans come to naught for lack of counsel, those greedy of gain and their pride brings destruction to their house.  

*The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the upright is his delight.*

*The Lord is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.*

Having God on your side, accepting your prayers, working in your life is a treasure beyond measure. The wicked and their public display of piety, their self-righteous works and so-called fasts, the "sacrifices" they make, be it the Old Testament animal offerings, or the vows made today to "cut out sweets," or to "drink less" or whatever, are an abomination to the Lord. 

*The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility*. The wicked may have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge. They lack the humility that comes before wisdom. 

**Romans 10:3**
*For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

The humility of submitting to His righteousness, the fear of the Lord, that we may gain understanding, being willing to receive reproof and correction, to seek after knowledge and study to be approved before God, that we may have a ready answer to all for our hope, this is the wisdom and the way we must seek. 

*The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.*

The promises of God towards His children are unfailing. That in our house will be much treasure, but not necessarily riches and wealth of this world. So rejoice! 

Our days with a merry heart are a continual feast. *Better is little with fear of the Lord than great treasure and trouble* *therewith*, Solomon writes. *Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith*. 

The slothful fool's way is made harder, like a hedge of thorns to get through. The wicked and greedy see their own destruction and live in constant fear and trouble. 

Choose the path of life. The way of God, by humbling yourself to His wisdom and hearing the instruction of your father, and bring that light to others. Be a wise son:

*A wise son maketh a glad father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother*.
